clock_and_reset_waveform.ACLK: Single rising-edge clock per AXI interface.
clock_and_reset_waveform.ARESETn: Active LOW. Async assert; sync deassert. After ARESETn=HIGH, earliest rising ACLK edge that the master may drive VALID HIGH is one cycle later (see Figure A3-1 'Exit from reset').

handshake_waveforms.sequence: Source asserts VALID; destination later asserts READY; transfer on next ACLK rising edge.
Destination asserts READY; source later asserts VALID; transfer on next ACLK rising edge.
Both asserted in same cycle; transfer occurs on that rising ACLK edge.

arrows: RREADY -> next ARVALID (master can issue more)

write_AXI3.note: AXI3 BVALID depends only on W handshake + WLAST, NOT on AW handshake.

write_AXI4_AXI5.note: AXI4/AXI5 add an additional slave dependency on AW handshake before BVALID, so slaves never need to buffer write data without the address.

max_outstanding_rules.same_ID_ordering: All transactions with the same AXI ID must remain in order (request order = response order).
max_outstanding_rules.different_ID_reordering: Transactions with different IDs may be reordered by the interconnect or slave.
max_outstanding_rules.different_ID_ordering: No ordering constraint between different IDs.
max_outstanding_rules.implementation_defined_max: Maximum outstanding transactions is implementation-defined per master+ID pair.
max_outstanding_rules.no_outstanding_count_in_spec: Spec defines no maximum number of outstanding transactions; an implementation-defined value.
max_outstanding_rules.read_response_ordering: Read data for the same ARID is returned in order.
max_outstanding_rules.read_reordering_depth: Implementation-defined; describes how many outstanding read transactions with different ARIDs may be in flight before the master needs to stall.
max_outstanding_rules.ahb: AHB-Lite is single-Manager; only one outstanding transfer at a time (no AXI-style outstanding queues). Pipelining means address phase of next transfer overlaps data phase of current transfer.
max_outstanding_rules.apb: APB has no pipelining; only one transfer in flight at a time; minimum 2 PCLK cycles per transfer.

narrow_transfer_waveforms: Narrow-bus transfers (transfer width < bus width) use the address+size pair to determine byte lanes per beat; refer to spec figure for example with 5-beat 8-bit incrementing burst on a 32-bit data bus.
write_response_dependency_rules: AXI3: BVALID may be asserted as soon as W handshake completes + WLAST=1, even before AW handshake.
AXI4/AXI5: BVALID may only be asserted after BOTH (AW handshake AND W handshake with WLAST=1) complete.
Same-ID write transactions: BRESP must follow same-AWID order of acceptance.

clock_and_reset_waveform_ahb.HCLK: Single rising-edge clock per AHB interface.
clock_and_reset_waveform_ahb.HRESETn: Active LOW; the only active-LOW signal in AHB.

clock_and_reset_waveform_apb.PCLK: Rising edge times all APB transfers.
clock_and_reset_waveform_apb.PRESETn: Active LOW; normally tied to system bus reset.

sequence: T0: Manager drives HADDR=A, HWRITE=0; HREADY=1.
T1: Subordinate samples address+control on rising HCLK.
T2: Subordinate drives HRDATA=Data(A); Manager samples on T3.
Address phase of next transfer overlaps data phase.

ahb_waited_transfer_waveform.case: Read transfer with two wait states (Figure 3-3)
sequence: One-cycle address phase.
Data phase extended over three cycles: HREADY=0, 0, then 1 with HRDATA=Data(A).
Address phase of next transfer also extended.
Cycle 1: HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=0.
Cycle 2: HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=1.
Manager option: continue burst OR drive HTRANS=IDLE during the 2-cycle ERROR to cancel.
T0-T1: NONSEQ at 0x20.
T1-T2: BUSY at 0x24.
T2-T3: SEQ at 0x24 (Manager continues).
T3-T4: SEQ at 0x28.
T4-T5: SEQ at 0x2C with wait state (HREADY=0).
T5-T6: data of 0x28 returns.
Cycle 1: NONSEQ read, HMASTLOCK=1, HADDR=A.
Cycle 2: NONSEQ write, HMASTLOCK=1, HADDR=A.
Cycle 3: IDLE, HMASTLOCK=0.
T0-T1: IDLE (PSEL=0, PENABLE=0).
T1: PADDR=Addr1, PWRITE=1, PSEL=1, PWDATA=Data1 — SETUP.
T2: PENABLE=1, PREADY=1 — ACCESS; transfer completes.
T3: bus may go IDLE or directly to next SETUP.
SETUP at T1.
ACCESS at T2 with PREADY=0.
ACCESS at T3 with PREADY=0.
ACCESS at T4 with PREADY=1 — transfer completes.
SETUP at T1, ACCESS at T2 with PREADY=0.
ACCESS at T3 with PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=1 — error signaled.
After T3: bus returns to IDLE.

edges: SETUP -> ACCESS unconditional next rising PCLK
ACCESS -> IDLE on PREADY=1 + no further transfer
ACCESS -> SETUP on PREADY=1 + back-to-back transfer

interconnect_combination_rules.ahb_HREADY_chain: Multiplexor combines all Subordinate HREADYOUTs into a single global HREADY broadcast (Figure 4-2). HRDATA / HRESP / HEXOKAY mux'd by decoder HSEL.
interconnect_combination_rules.ahb_apb_bridge: AHB-to-APB bridge is an AHB Subordinate + APB Manager; PSLVERR -> HRESP=ERROR.
